reason: Sunlight can lift ocean water through evaporation, a likely first step in keeping water travelling.
expectation: The Sun will warm the ocean and produce water vapour or a cloud.

effect: Evaporation provides water vapour for the next stage of the water cycle.
reaction: The detail that dissolved salts stay behind is useful.
reason: Air may cool and carry the evaporated water, helping it form clouds.
expectation: The water vapour will form clouds or otherwise move through the atmosphere.

effect: Clouds have formed from cooling moist air, providing a likely source of rain.
reaction: The distinction between invisible vapour and visible droplets is useful.
reason: Clouds can bring precipitation to the land, moving water toward rivers.
expectation: Rain will fall on the land, perhaps beginning runoff.

effect: Clouds combined with Water to produce rainfall, so water can now move across the land.
reaction: I expected the crust to trigger rain, so the automatic combination with Water was a surprise.
reason: Rainfall on the stone crust could produce runoff toward rivers.
expectation: Water will flow over the land, beginning runoff or a river.

effect: Rainfall on the crust created rivers, which can carry sediment toward the ocean.
reaction: The explanation of rivers changing their routes through erosion and deposition is useful.
reason: Rivers meeting the ocean can deposit sediment and build a delta.
expectation: The rivers will deposit sediment at their mouths, forming a delta.

effect: Rivers cannot combine directly with the ocean; Earth and Sun are the available partners.
reaction: The compatibility feedback clarifies the next options.
reason: Earth is a likely source of sediment for building a delta.
expectation: The rivers will carry or deposit sediment, potentially forming a delta.

alternatives.reason: Sunlight might help keep water travelling, but the delta goal suggests trying Earth first.

effect: Rivers and Earth produced sediment, which can build a delta where flowing water slows.
reaction: The link between erosion upstream and building elsewhere is satisfying.
reason: Sediment deposited where rivers meet the ocean can form a delta.
expectation: The sediment will accumulate at the coast and form a delta.

alternatives.reason: The rivers carry the sediment, so they might be the required partner instead.

effect: Sediment combined with Rivers to form a delta, completing that goal; keeping water travelling remains.
reaction: The branching channels make the sediment's role in building land clear.
reason: Rivers can combine with Sun, as the earlier compatibility feedback showed, and sunlight powers the water cycle.
expectation: Sunlight will return some river water to the atmosphere, helping keep the water cycle moving.

effect: The Sun and Rivers completed the water cycle and the chapter, tying evaporation, precipitation and runoff together.
reaction: The division of roles between solar energy and gravity is a satisfying summary.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the delta was worthwhile: it connected erosion and sediment transport to the formation of new land and branching channels.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying Rivers with Ocean was less worthwhile because the intuitive pairing failed and only revealed the available partners.

surprise.text: Clouds would not combine with Stone crust; the feedback automatically combined them with Water to make rainfall instead.

arbitrary.text: Using Water with Clouds to trigger rainfall felt somewhat arbitrary: I expected clouds meeting land to produce rain, though the result explained droplets growing heavy enough to fall.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the chapter made water-cycle processes and land formation understandable through connected discoveries, despite a couple of unintuitive pairings.
